newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN DEALERS' BODY TO FINE NOMURA SEC 100 MLN YEN.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN DEALERS' BODY TO FINE NOMURA SEC 100 MLN YEN.

text.p: The Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) said on Friday it had decided to levy a fine of 100 million yen on Nomura Securities Co Ltd for its part in illegal payoffs to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer.

The JSDA, a self-regulatory body of the securities industry, also said in a statement that it decided to change its rules to require brokerages to cut ties with what it called "anti-social interests", such as corporate racketeers, and to ban deals with customers under assumed names.

The body has also urged 25 brokerages which list their shares on stock exchanges to work out measures to avoid dealing with corporate racketeers and called on all member brokerages to improve internal supervision and management policies to ensure compliance with laws and industry rules, it said.
The JSDA also said it is considering an increase in the maximum fine it imposes against brokerages from the present 100 million yen.

On Wednesday, Nomura was required to suspend part of its operations under administrative penalties for making illegal payoffs to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer. Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) was also ordered to suspend some of its operations for its involvement in the scandal.

The penalties against Nomura included a halt to stock and stock-related business at all branches from August 6 to August 12. Nomura has also been ordered to halt stock dealing on its own account until the end of the year.

In the wake of the racketeer payoff scandal, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto instructed the Finance and Justice ministries in June to work on beefing up penalties. An advisory body to the finance minister also urged regulators to impose harsher penalties for illegal stock transactions.
